items.summary: Both me and my cofounder are in high school, and we're currently building Powermove, a video-editing tool that connects to an AI agent, letting users modify the app featureset, and generate effects and extensions. We think this is the next step when it comes to software. We're already starting to see it, especially since a similar feature was just added recently in Claude Code. We believe that it will prove most useful in creative software though, and allow creatives to make essentially anything they want. As a motion designer myself with a few years of experience, it has already turbocharged my outputs. The video you're seeing above was only possible with Powermove. It's also completely free and open source.

Show HN: Personal Agent Proxy (Open Source)
items.summary: Every (personal) agent (like Muse, Instinct, Grokbot, Poke) asks you to connect your email, calendar, and tools again. Permissions are intransparent and every provider ends up building the same integrations. We think there needs to be an independent tool that holds all connections to third party companies. That way you can keep auth separate, audit what an agent does, set fine-grained permissions and easily switch between the agent apps. I built this over the last few days with my friend Konsti. It's open source and we’ve put a lot of care into the self-hosting experience. Now my Instinct has the same tools as Claude Code and Codex on my laptop. What are your thoughts about this and how are you handling this today?
